Hi Megan,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a compact feature matrix and an updated SOW that shows two packaging options (Compact and Full). Quick summary up front so it's easier for your procurement review: 

- Compact: 20 seats, core generation + embeddings, basic support, annual commit. Recommended for pilot-to-production.
- Full: 20 seats + advanced routing, priority support, 24/7 SLAs, optional dedicated capacity.

We're prepared to offer a 10% platform discount on an annual commit for the Compact package. Regarding downgrade/flexibility: we can permit a single downgrade in the first 90 days with prorated credit back to the account, or a 30-day interchangeable grace for seat adjustments if you prefer more operational flexibility — I wanted to surface both for you.

Please see attached 'Acme_Feature_Matrix_v1.xlsx' and 'Acme_SOW_v2.pdf' for the line-item details and the SOW. Would you like us to map a couple of concrete pricing scenarios for Procurement (annual vs quarterly, and a version with a downgrade credit)? If so, I can send those by EOD tomorrow.

If easier, happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through trade-offs.

1) Can you outline the downgrade credit math? Specifically: if we commit annually and then reduce seats or throughput mid-term, what is the credit calculation (proration by days, full month, or token-based)?
2) If we stay in Compact but need an additional feature from Full (e.g., priority routing), can that be add-on priced or does it require a re-tier?

Also: Procurement requested sample pricing scenarios (annual commit @10% discount vs quarterly @5%), and a fallback where we can retreat seats with minimal penalty. Can you provide those as a simple matrix we can attach to our internal approval packet?

Finally, can you attach the SOC2 section we referenced? Engineering wants the control mapping before sign-off.

My thoughts / suggested responses to include in our matrix: 
- Downgrade credit: prorate by remaining whole months in the billing cycle (simple for accounting), with an upfront admin fee equal to 1 month of seats for mid-term downgrades if they want unlimited rollback flexibility. Alternatively, no admin fee but limit downgrades to 1 per 12 months. 
- Feature add-on: priority routing and advanced observability can be sold as monthly add-ons to Compact at a per-seat uplift (recommended). Avoid forcing a full tier change unless they need dedicated capacity.
- Feature parity: we can guarantee behavior for 60 days post-downgrade (cached prefixes & routing fallbacks kept); beyond that, features are not guaranteed without a re-upgrade. 

Concessions I'm willing to consider to close: 
- Option: Annual commit 20 seats at 10% + 30-day downgrade credit (prorated by month) + 10% one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice).
- Counter: If they insist on unlimited downgrade windows, step discount to 8% (and remove onboarding credit).

I attached a quick pricing scenarios workbook 'Acme_pricing_scenarios.xlsx' with three rows (annual/quarterly/quarter-with-downgrade). Recommend we present Annual (A) and Quarterly (B) side-by-side to Procurement.

Thoughts? Lauren/Karthik — any legal/accounting flags here?

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi Megan / Procurement team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal review, here are concrete options you can include in the packet. I kept the math simple for Procurement and Accounting.

Option A — Annual Compact (recommended)
- 20-seat annual commit
- 10% platform discount (applied to subscription line)
- Downgrade allowance: one downgrade in the first 90 days; credit = remaining whole months prorated on the subscription line (example shown in attached workbook).
- Add-ons: priority routing and advanced observability available as monthly per-seat add-ons (no tier swap required).
- Onboarding: 10% onboarding credit applied to first invoice.

Option B — Quarterly Flex
- Quarterly billing, 20-seat minimum per quarter
- 5% platform discount
- Downgrade: seat reductions allowed at quarter boundary only (no mid-quarter prorate)

Trade-offs: Annual gives best unit economics + one flexible downgrade window; Quarterly provides operational flexibility at a higher price. If Procurement needs unlimited mid-term downgrades we can offer that but would reduce the discount to 8% and remove onboarding credit.

Attachments included: 'Acme_pricing_scenarios.xlsx' with worked examples + 'Acme_SOW_v2.pdf' and the SOC2 Excerpt (see link below).

- If you want the 9am PT call Friday, I'm available and will have finance & legal on standby.
